import sys, json, re, datetime, posixpath

# THE INDEX OF A LIBRARIAN (librarian, GH #950). One librarian per knowledge
# space: a catalogue of every source the space holds -- its path, kind,
# format, summary line, tags and the names of its top-level items -- kept
# current from the space's own announcements, so that `find` (cell `./query`)
# answers "where is the thing called X" without waking a single file.
#
# A SOURCE ANNOUNCES, THE INDEX PULLS. A node source (a file space: `fh-`;
# reserved: `ob-`) emits `source_changed` {source, version, path, fmt, parser,
# mark, nodes, links, tomb} after every move of a head. The index writes the
# path, the format and the announced version at once (`entries.announced`) and
# sends exactly two requests on `pull`: ONE `info` (the kind) and ONE
# `outline` (the top-level names). A constant number of hops per
# announcement, whatever the size of the source. A move (same version, new
# path) is the same announcement: the path comes ONLY from the event, because
# events arrive in order and a late `info` of an earlier announcement would
# carry the old path.
# Events are written in the order they arrive because this cell runs one
# message at a time (`params.max_concurrency` 1, as the curator's compose
# since GH #765): with the dispatcher's default of four, two announcements of
# one source ran side by side and the older one could be written last.
#
# A STALE PULL NEVER OVERWRITES. Every answer is written with `announced == v`
# in its `where` -- a compare-and-set on the version it pulled. An answer that
# arrives after a newer announcement matches no row and changes nothing; there
# is no table of pulls in flight, and an answer that never comes leaves no row
# behind (the entry keeps the path and format of its announcement).
#
# THE DESCRIPTION COMES LATER, ON ITS OWN EVENT. A file space announces a head
# before its model has summarised it, so an `info` pulled on the announcement
# carries the summary line of the version before (or none). The space emits
# `source_described` {source, version, path, oneline, tags} once the summary
# of a head is written, and the summary line and the tags come from there
# only -- written with `announced == version`, so the description of a version
# that is no longer announced changes nothing (GH #950, OR-BC-68).
#
# NO DELETE. A removal (`{source, path, tomb: true}`, no version) turns the row
# into a grave (`tomb` '1', `announced` emptied so every pull still in flight
# turns stale); `find` reads living rows only. A source that comes back is the
# same row again.
#
# THE WORDS OF A ROW. `pterms` and `nterms` are the path and the names cut by
# `terms()` -- word runs split at case boundaries (`fooBar` -> foobar foo bar,
# `HTTPServer` -> httpserver http server) -- because the full-text index splits
# on punctuation only and a question for `server` has to find `HTTPServer`.
# `terms()` stands WORD FOR WORD in `./query`, which cuts a question with it.
#
# No model, no embedding request, no network: everything here is a pure
# function of what the source answered.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
P = doc.get("params") or {}
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}


def _int(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip()):
        return default
    try:
        return int(float(v))
    except Exception:
        return default


NAMES_MAX = max(1, _int("names_max", 64))

ME = "index"
FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
PARTS = ("info", "outline")
OUTLINE_MAX = 2000
ONELINE_MAX = 300
TAGS_MAX = 8
SOURCE_RE = re.compile(r"^(fh|ob)-[0-9a-f]{12}$")
VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{4,64}$")


# ============================================================ PURE: WORDS

RUN_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W_]+")


def split_case(run):
    """One word run cut at its case boundaries: a lower (or a digit) before an
    upper (`fooBar`, `utf8Decode`), and the last upper of an upper run before
    a lower (`HTTPServer`). Digits stay with the word they follow."""
    out, cur = [], ""
    for i, ch in enumerate(run):
        if cur and ch.isupper():
            prev = run[i - 1]
            nxt = run[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(run) else ""
            if not prev.isupper() or nxt.islower():
                out.append(cur)
                cur = ""
        cur += ch
    if cur:
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def terms(text):
    """The words of a text, lower case, in order, each once: every word run
    (`[^\\W_]+`, unicode) and, when it falls into more than one part at its
    case boundaries, the whole run first (`fooBar` -> foobar, foo, bar)."""
    out, seen = [], set()
    for run in RUN_RE.findall(str(text or "")):
        parts = split_case(run)
        toks = ([run] if len(parts) > 1 else []) + parts
        for t in toks:
            t = t.lower()
            if t and t not in seen:
                seen.add(t)
                out.append(t)
    return out


def dir_of(path):
    """The folder a path sits in: `/pkg/a.py` -> `/pkg`, `/a` -> `/`."""
    p = str(path or "")
    parent = posixpath.dirname(p)
    if parent:
        return parent
    return "/" if p.startswith("/") else ""


# ============================================================ PURE: NAMES

PCT_RE = re.compile(r"(?:%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+")
DUP_RE = re.compile(r"~[0-9]+$")


def pct_decode(s):
    """`%XX` sequences as UTF-8 (the file space percent-encodes `%`, `#`, `@`
    and whitespace in a name). By hand, with no URL library: the egress sweep
    (gh144) reads any URL module in a script as network I/O."""
    return PCT_RE.sub(lambda m: bytes.fromhex(m.group(0).replace("%", ""))
                      .decode("utf-8", "replace"), str(s))


def anchor_names(anchor):
    """The names one anchor gives a reader: the part after the first `:` of
    its last `/` segment, percent-decoded (`def:load` -> load, `sec:setup` ->
    setup, `key:/server` -> server); `impl:T+Tr` names both `T` and `Tr`; a
    `page:<n>` names nothing. A repeat's `~2` is no part of the name."""
    seg = str(anchor or "").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    if ":" in seg:
        kind, name = seg.split(":", 1)
    else:
        kind, name = "", seg
    if kind == "page":
        return []
    name = DUP_RE.sub("", name)
    parts = name.split("+") if kind == "impl" else [name]
    return [n for n in (pct_decode(x).strip() for x in parts) if n]


def top_names(nodes, cap):
    """The names of an outline's top-level nodes (`parent` empty), in outline
    order, each once, at most `cap`."""
    out, seen = [], set()
    for n in nodes if isinstance(nodes, list) else []:
        if not isinstance(n, dict) or str(n.get("parent") or ""):
            continue
        for name in anchor_names(n.get("anchor")):
            if name not in seen:
                seen.add(name)
                out.append(name)
                if len(out) >= cap:
                    return out
    return out


def tags_of(v):
    """`tags` of a `source_described` event as a JSON list: a list of strings, at most
    eight; anything else is no tags."""
    if isinstance(v, list) and all(isinstance(t, str) for t in v):
        return json.dumps([t.strip() for t in v if t.strip()][:TAGS_MAX], ensure_ascii=False)
    return "[]"


# ============================================================ PURE: OPS

def v12(v):
    return str(v or "")[:12]


def truthy(v):
    return v is True or (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and v != 0) or \
        (isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"))


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)


def count(v):
    try:
        return max(0, int(v or 0))
    except Exception:
        return 0


def op_id_of(part, S, v):
    return "lib:f:i:%s:%s:%s" % (part, S, v)


def parse_op_id(op_id):
    """`lib:f:i:<part>:<source>:<v12>` -> (part, source, version), or None."""
    bits = str(op_id or "").split(":")
    if len(bits) != 6 or bits[:3] != ["lib", "f", "i"] or bits[3] not in PARTS \
            or not SOURCE_RE.match(bits[4]) or not VERSION_RE.match(bits[5]):
        return None
    return bits[3], bits[4], bits[5]


def tomb_ops(S, stamp):
    """A removal, in one bundle: the row turns into a grave; never a delete."""
    return [("e-tomb", {"operation": "update", "table": "entries",
                        "set": {"tomb": "1", "announced": "", "changed_at": stamp},
                        "where": {"source": S}})]


def announce_ops(S, v, path, fmt, nodes, stamp):
    """An announcement, in one bundle: the row of a new source (the insert
    meets the unique index on a known one, which is expected), then the
    announced version, path and format of every source."""
    pterms = " ".join(terms(path))
    row = {"source": S, "path": path, "dir": dir_of(path), "kind": "", "fmt": fmt,
           "oneline": "", "tags": "[]", "names": "[]", "nodes": str(nodes),
           "version": "", "announced": v, "changed_at": stamp, "tomb": "",
           "pterms": pterms, "nterms": ""}
    return [("e-ins", {"operation": "insert", "table": "entries", "row": row}),
            ("e-upd", {"operation": "update", "table": "entries",
                       "set": {"announced": v, "path": path, "dir": dir_of(path), "fmt": fmt,
                               "pterms": pterms, "nodes": str(nodes), "tomb": "",
                               "changed_at": stamp},
                       "where": {"source": S}})]


def pull_requests(S, v, nodes):
    """The two requests of one announcement, as (hop, body). No `caller`."""
    file = S + "@" + v
    asks = (("info", {"version": v}),
            ("outline", {"version": v, "limit": max(1, min(nodes, OUTLINE_MAX))}))
    return [({"route": "pull", "op": part, "op_id": op_id_of(part, S, v)},
             {"op": part, "file": file, "source": S, "version": v, "args": args})
            for part, args in asks]


def info_ops(S, v, ans, stamp):
    """An `info` answer -> its one compare-and-set update: the kind only. Its
    `oneline` is not taken -- on an announcement the summary of that version
    is not written yet (see `described_ops`)."""
    return [("e-info", {"operation": "update", "table": "entries",
                        "set": {"kind": str(ans.get("kind") or ""), "version": v,
                                "changed_at": stamp},
                        "where": {"source": S, "announced": v}})]


def described_ops(S, v, ev, stamp):
    """A `source_described` event -> its one compare-and-set update: summary
    line and tags, only while `v` is the announced version. The path of the
    event is not taken: the path comes from `source_changed` alone."""
    return [("e-desc", {"operation": "update", "table": "entries",
                        "set": {"oneline": str(ev.get("oneline") or "")[:ONELINE_MAX],
                                "tags": tags_of(ev.get("tags")), "changed_at": stamp},
                        "where": {"source": S, "announced": v}})]


def outline_ops(S, v, ans, stamp, cap):
    """An `outline` answer -> its one compare-and-set update."""
    names = top_names(ans.get("nodes"), cap)
    return [("e-names", {"operation": "update", "table": "entries",
                         "set": {"names": json.dumps(names, ensure_ascii=False),
                                 "nterms": " ".join(terms(" ".join(names))), "version": v,
                                 "changed_at": stamp},
                         "where": {"source": S, "announced": v}})]


# ============================================================ PLUMBING

def emit(msgs):
    for m in msgs:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and not any(k in m for k in ("messages", "system", "attachments")):
            m["messages"] = []
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("librarian/index: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def store(ops, phase, carry):
    return {"header": {"route": "index_store", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": ME,
                       "cur_call": json.dumps(carry, sort_keys=True)},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    out = {}
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "error_code": ""}
    results = body.get("results")
    if isinstance(results, list):
        for r in results:
            if isinstance(r, dict):
                leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                                     {"payload": None, "error_code": ""})
                leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
    elif len(out) == 1:
        next(iter(out.values()))["error_code"] = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
    return out


# ============================================================ LANES

lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")
phase = str(ctx.get("cur_phase") or "")
op_ = str(hop.get("operation") or "")

if lane == "source_changed":
    S = str(d.get("source") or "").strip()
    if not SOURCE_RE.match(S):
        park("source_changed without a source address -- dropped")
    stamp = now()
    if truthy(d.get("tomb")):
        emit([store(tomb_ops(S, stamp), "tomb", {"source": S})])
    version = str(d.get("version") or "").strip().lower()
    if not VERSION_RE.match(version):
        park("source_changed without a version -- dropped")
    v = v12(version)
    path = str(d.get("path") or "")
    nodes = count(d.get("nodes"))
    msgs = [store(announce_ops(S, v, path, str(d.get("fmt") or ""), nodes, stamp),
                  "announce", {"source": S, "version": v})]
    for h, b in pull_requests(S, v, nodes):
        b["header"] = h
        msgs.append(b)
    emit(msgs)

if lane == "source_described":
    S = str(d.get("source") or "").strip()
    version = str(d.get("version") or "").strip().lower()
    if not SOURCE_RE.match(S) or not VERSION_RE.match(version):
        park("source_described without a source address and a version -- dropped")
    v = v12(version)
    emit([store(described_ops(S, v, d, now()), "described", {"source": S, "version": v})])

if lane == "in_pulled":
    got = parse_op_id(hop.get("op_id"))
    if not got:
        park("in_pulled under a foreign op_id %r -- dropped" % str(hop.get("op_id") or ""))
    part, S, v = got
    if d.get("ok") is not True:
        sys.stderr.write("librarian/index: %s of %s@%s not readable (%s) -- left as it was\n"
                         % (part, S, v, json.dumps(d.get("error"))))
        emit([])
    stamp = now()
    ops = info_ops(S, v, d, stamp) if part == "info" else outline_ops(S, v, d, stamp, NAMES_MAX)
    emit([store(ops, part, {"source": S, "version": v})])

if lane:
    park("unknown lane %r -- dropped" % lane)
if not op_:
    park("a message with neither a lane nor a store answer -- dropped")

# A store answer: every phase is one bundle and ends here. Only the insert of
# an announcement may fail (the unique index on a known source).
lg = legs(d)
bad = sorted(c for c, leg in lg.items() if leg["error_code"] and c != "e-ins")
if bad:
    sys.stderr.write("librarian/index: store refused %s in phase %s\n"
                     % (", ".join(bad), phase or "?"))
emit([])

names_max.description: The most top-level names one source keeps in the catalogue (`names`, `nterms`); an outline with more is cut, in outline order.

description.purpose: Keeps the catalogue current: an announcement (`source_changed`) writes path, folder, format and the announced version in one bundle and pulls one `info` (the kind) and one `outline` of that version; a `source_described` brings the summary line and the tags; each answer is written by compare-and-set on the announced version, so a stale pull never overwrites a newer one. A `tomb` turns the row into a grave.
description.use_when: Inside a librarian only, behind `source_changed`, `source_described` and the `in_pulled` answers whose `op_id` starts with `lib:f:i:`.
description.not_in_scope: No question (`./query`), no model, no network, no content of a source beyond its summary line, no delete.
description.emits_meaning: `index_store` to `./store` (one bundle per announcement or answer), `pull` (two per announcement) out of the hive.
description.consumes_meaning: An announcement, a description, a source's answer to a pull, and the store's answers to its own bundles.
